title: Silently Ignoring Trailing Junk during String Parsing
pattern: Extracting and parsing a valid prefix from a string while silently ignoring trailing unparsed characters.
why_bad: It hides bad input data, leading to garbage-in-garbage-out bugs or security vulnerabilities (e.g., bypassing network bounds because `"8080/admin"` was parsed as simply `"8080"`).
detection: Regexes or custom iterator chains that extract matching prefixes and discard the rest of the string without asserting that the remainder is empty or valid.
counterexample:
Intentionally parsing a streaming token stream where a remainder is expected:
```rust
fn parse_next_token(input: &str) -> Option<(Token, &str)> { ... }
```
source: *Type-driven Development with Idris* by Edwin Brady (p. 70, 163).
